flag_meanings.o2_not_numeric: The oxygen cell holds a label (e.g. RAMP, LOW O2), not a single number.
flag_meanings.o2_not_in_table: The source table has no oxygen column.
flag_meanings.o2_approximate: The source gives oxygen as an approximate value (written with ~).
flag_meanings.o2_range: The source gives oxygen as a range; see o2_fraction_min and o2_fraction_max.
flag_meanings.pressure_missing: The pressure cell is blank or zero.
flag_meanings.pressure_not_numeric: The pressure cell is not a number.
flag_meanings.pressure_not_in_table: The source table has no pressure column.
flag_meanings.fuel_from_row_above: The material cell is blank (merged cell in the source); filled from the row above.
flag_meanings.duplicate_row: Every cell of this row is identical to an earlier row of the same table.
flag_meanings.airflow_negative_in_source: The source records a negative air rate; kept as written. Its meaning is not stated, so leave it out of airflow ranges (airflowRange() in data/load.ts does).
flag_meanings.material_not_stated: The material cell names a shape or size (e.g. '2 cm sphere', '1/4" black rod') but not the material, so fuel_material is null.
flag_meanings.time_not_recorded: The time cell holds no time (e.g. 'Ku LOS', 'no ku', 'n/a') or an unclear format such as '1744'; the cell is kept as written in source_extra.
flag_meanings.burn_time_from_gmt_times: burn_time_s is the table's GMT flame-off time minus its GMT ignition time.
flag_meanings.dimensions_swapped_in_source: The table lists length 40.6 cm and width 94 cm. NASA's Saffire fact sheet gives the sample as 0.4 m wide by 1 m long (and the SAFFIRE-III table agrees), so sample_length_cm and sample_width_cm are given the right way round. source_extra keeps the table as written.
flag_meanings.thickness_typo_suspected: The thickness cell reads '037 mm' (probably 0.37 mm). Not corrected: sample_thickness_mm is null.
flag_meanings.value_not_single: A dimension cell holds more than one value or a reference (e.g. '0.85 and 0.37 mm', 'See Fig. 5'), so the typed field is null; the cell is kept in source_extra.
flag_meanings.burning_rate_unit_unclear: NASA's header gives the burning-rate unit only as 'mm'; part of the unit may have been lost in the file. The number is kept as written.
flag_meanings.pressure_from_report: The table has no pressure; NASA's report states one for these tests (pressure_source gives the report, page and words). Checked by hand; see data_sourced/solid_conditions.json.
flag_meanings.pressure_range_from_report: NASA's report gives a pressure range for these tests (pressure_atm_min / max, with pressure_source); no single value, so the test is not placed on the map.
flag_meanings.pressure_range_from_sensor_log: NASA's sensor log for this burn records ambient pressure in PSIA; pressure_atm_min / max is its range over the log (pressure_source says where). No single value, so the test is not placed on the map.
flag_meanings.conditions_from_test_matrix: The table has no oxygen or pressure; both come from NASA's BASS as-run test matrix ('ISS environment' columns), matched on As Run Test #, Test # and Sample # (pressure_source gives the cells). They describe the test session's atmosphere, not a reading during the burn. See data_sourced/bass_conditions.json.
flag_meanings.o2_diluted_work_volume: A nitrogen-diluted BASS test: the oxygen is the glovebox work volume after NASA added nitrogen, calculated by NASA (its notes say e.g. 'Calc 17.07% O2'), not ISS cabin air.
flag_meanings.o2_differs_from_test_sheet: NASA's per-test sheet for this test gives a different oxygen value (after the colon) from the table's. The table's value is kept; NASA does not say which is right. See data_sourced/table_conflicts.json.
flag_meanings.o2_from_sensor_log: NASA's sensor log for this burn records oxygen (%); o2_sensor_min / max is its range over the log. The table's own oxygen value, if any, is kept unchanged.
flag_meanings.o2_differs_from_sensor_log: The table's oxygen and the sensor log's oxygen for this burn do not overlap (e.g. 21.5-21.7 % against 22.2-22.7 %). NASA does not say which is right.
flag_meanings.extinction_diameter_above_initial: The extinction diameter is a little larger than the initial droplet diameter (by no more than the table's 0.01 mm step, in a flame that went out within a second). Kept as written.
flag_meanings.shape_not_stated: Neither the test's own columns nor a NASA document we checked states the fuel's shape, so fuel_shape is null (fuel_size_text may still give a size the row states).
flag_meanings.temperature_placeholder: The peak burner temperature cell holds a placeholder ('-', '#VALUE!', or 273.15 K beside an empty Celsius cell), so peak_burner_temp_c is null.
